text:
maria_sales: Heads up — NessieBank sent a security request asking for an ISO/ISMS applicability statement for the POC. They want explicit scope, which controls are in/out, subcontractor/KMS commitments, and any contract language that affects data residency. They asked for this by EOD Friday.

alex_security: Which contract are they referencing? POC addendum or the MSA? We should confirm whether they mean the demo environment or production-level POC. Also we should note what evidence they want (SoA, policy URLs, sample configs).

sam_engineer: For the usual POC we use hosted Redwood API. Quick scoping note:
```
POC_SCOPE = "inference runtime, API gateway, customer request/response payloads"
IN_SCOPE_SERVICES = ["runtime", "api", "logs (30d)"]
OUT_OF_SCOPE = ["dev laptops", "CI systems"]
```
If they require data residency or KMS separation, we need Dedicated or Private — that changes deployment and timeline.

chris_product: Draft applicability text we can start with (feel free to edit):
```
Redwood Inference confirms that for the NessieBank POC the ISMS scope is limited to the inference serving runtime, API boundary, and associated logging/monitoring infrastructure used to process test data. Development environments, upstream CI/CD pipelines, and third-party developer tools are explicitly out of scope for the POC. Where customer-provided keys or controlled residency are required, Redwood will provision Dedicated or Private deployment per contract.
```
Notes: call out subcontractor use (we use cloud providers + telemetry vendor) and state we can provide subprocessors list on request.

maria_sales: Thanks — two quick asks from me: 1) does this scope language satisfy a buyer asking for ISO alignment (general question), and 2) what is the cost/pricing delta if we have to move to Dedicated for the POC?

alex_security: 1) Yes, that wording is fine as a short applicability statement; we should also produce a short SoA table mapping relevant Annex A controls to Redwood artifacts (policy doc links, config screenshots, evidence types). 2) Pricing: Dedicated trial is possible but baseline committed pricing is higher — rough ballpark: +30-60% on monthly unit cost depending on capacity. We can offer a limited-time Dedicated trial credit for sales-qualified deals.

sam_engineer: For evidence/timeline: we can assemble a minimal packet with policy links (Acceptable Use, Access Control, Cryptography), architecture diagram, and a sample KMS config within ~3 business days for hosted POC. If they require Dedicated/Private and customer KMS, add 5-7 business days to provision and validate.

chris_product: Also flag the contract clause about subcontractors: our standard POC addendum includes subprocessors and a commitment to notify customers about changes. If NessieBank needs a no-subcontractors clause, that's a major blocker and needs legal review.

maria_sales: @alex_security can you draft the SoA spreadsheet tomorrow? @sam_engineer can you prepare the tech scoping + provisioning timeline? @chris_product can you prepare the short applicability snippet for legal review? I'll ask legal to look at the subcontractor clause once we have the draft. Sync tomorrow 10:00am PT? :calendar: :white_check_mark:

alex_security: On it — I’ll put a SoA draft in the shared folder by EOD tomorrow and include which evidence we can provide as artifacts.

sam_engineer: I’ll add estimated provisioning steps and a short checklist for Dedicated vs Hosted to the doc.

legal-bot: :robot_face: POC addendum template uploaded: https://redwood.internal/documents/poc-addendum-template (internal). If you need an exception request for subprocessors, file a Legal Intake with tag "POC-Subproc".

maria_sales: Great — thanks everyone. If NessieBank insists on data residency + customer-managed KMS we should surface the pricing delta immediately and offer the Dedicated trial credit to keep momentum. Will update after tomorrow's sync. :thumbsup:
